findings.title: Light theme color unintentionally changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: The original value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for `.topic-meta-data h5 a`. The new code uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The first argument to `dark-light-choose` (used in light themes) should preserve the original 30% lightness, but it was changed to 70%. This will make the username links in embedded post metadata significantly lighter/washed out in light themes.

findings.title: Light theme color for .group-member-info .name unintentionally changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for `.group-member-info .name`. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme branch should remain at 30% to avoid a visual regression, but it was changed to 50%, making the group member name lighter than intended in light themes.

findings.title: Light theme color for .group-member-info .name unintentionally changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Same issue as the desktop counterpart: the original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for `.group-member-info .name` was replaced with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`. The light-theme value should remain 30% to avoid changing the existing appearance.

findings.title: Light theme color for topic-map h3 unintentionally changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The original value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` for `.topic-map h3`. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme branch should preserve the original 20% lightness, but it was changed to 50%, making the topic map heading significantly lighter in light themes.

findings.title: Light theme color for .custom-message-length unintentionally changed from 70% to 30%
findings.body: The original value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` for `.custom-message-length`. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light-theme branch should preserve 70% but was changed to 30%, making the message length text much darker in light themes. It appears the light and dark values were accidentally swapped.
